content: Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin base and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation, may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of diazepam (buccal) by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the elimination rate of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of diazepam (intranasal) by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the elimination rate of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base may also decrease the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concurrent use. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of donepezil by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin liposomal by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with duvelisib increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing the risk of toxicities. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. Eliglustat increases the levels of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of the P-gp substrate and titrate to clinical effect. Eluxadoline increases the levels of erythromycin base by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Eluxadoline may increase the systemic exposure of co-administered OATP1B1 substrates. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of erythromycin base by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. Encorafenib affects the metabolism of erythromycin base by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Encorafenib, an OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor for signs and symptoms of increased exposure and consider adjusting the dose of these substrates. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels of eszopiclone by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Erythromycin base also increases the levels of eszopiclone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the eszopiclone starting dose to 1 mg/day. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of etoposide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of exemestane by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base and ezogabine both increase the risk of toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly when titrated to 1200 mg/day. The QT interval should be monitored when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. Erythromycin base and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the toxicity of fluvastatin by mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. Erythromycin base and fluvoxamine both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin base and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Concomitant use of fostamatinib may increase concentrations of P-gp substrates. Monitor for toxicities of the P-gp substrate drug that may require dosage reduction when given concurrently with fostamatinib. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Fostemsavir and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Gadobenate and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Gepirone and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3. Goserelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the FDA-approved labeling recommends reducing the guanfacine dosage to half of the recommended dose if co-administered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Histrelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin base increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. When co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily (for B-cell malignancies) or 420 mg daily (for graft-versus-host disease). After discontinuation of the CYP3A inhibitor, resume the previous dose of ibrutinib. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. The use of a CYP3A4 inhibitor may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. Erythromycin base and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases the levels of erythromycin base by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels of indacaterol (inhaled) by mechanisms involving modulation of both P-gp and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor. No dose adjustment is warranted at the 75 mcg dose. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Erythromycin base and insulin degludec increase the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor. Both drugs decrease blood glucose levels. Erythromycin base and insulin degludec/insulin aspart increase the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor. Both drugs decrease blood glucose levels.
